subject: EdgeFin: edgepool saturation causing throughput shortfall — exec decision needed
messages:
From: Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iyer@edgefin.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeFin SRE <sre@edgefin.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: production slowdown — high latency, 5xx/queueing since 08:50 PT

Mina —

We're seeing a sustained spike in latency and a burst of 5xx errors for our production inference endpoints starting ~08:50 PT. Client-side dashboards show request queues backing up and p99 latency jumping from ~120ms to >2.5s; errors are ~3.2% on calls routed to the dedicated pool you provisioned for us ("edgepool"). This is impacting our checkout path for ~10% of traffic.

We've attached a small sampling of logs and a queue snapshot. Can you confirm whether this is coming from your side (pool saturation) or if it's a model/SDK regression on our side? We need an ETA on mitigation — customers are calling.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Director of Engineering, EdgeFin

Attachments: edgefin-prod-sample-logs-20290611.zip (truncated), edgepool-queue-snapshot-0900.json

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: production slowdown — high latency, 5xx/queueing since 08:50 PT

Mina / team — quick technical triage after ingesting the provided snapshot and cross-referencing infra metrics:

Findings (prelim):
- Dedicated pool (edgepool) at 98% GPU utilization on nodes hosting short-sequence models; multiple hosts report KV cache churn.
- Spike correlates with an increase in small, high-QPS inference calls (pattern looks like many short-lived connections).
- Autoscaling did not trigger because the pool hit the reserved ceiling (reserved_qps cap) — we have capacity physically available but it's gated by the customer's reserved throughput and routing policy.
- Error surface: a rise in 429s (rate-limited) and downstream 5xx during queue overflow. p95/p99 latency numbers match Rajesh's report.

Immediate mitigations we can enact now (minutes):
1) Temporarily switch routing for a subset (10-20%) of EdgeFin traffic to a compatible hosted variant (quantized Llama-13B-q4f) to relieve pressure — requires exec approval for cross-tenant burst billing.
2) Enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for their hot prefixes (helps 30-40% of repeated calls).
3) Apply short-lived priority burst window (30 minutes) on this pool and allow overflow onto a shared fallback pool while we investigate noisy neighbor — still requires approval.

Longer term (hours):
- Re-evaluate reserved_qps sizing and recommend a phased increase with an SLA amendment + one-time burst credits.
- Work with EdgeFin SRE to tune client-side connection pooling to reduce short-lived connections.

I'll keep digging into kernel telemetry (quantization kernels) but current evidence points to policy-driven reserved throughput gating + increased connection churn.

David
Sr. Infra Engineer — Serving Runtime

> Client-side dashboards show request queues backing up and p99 latency jumping from ~120ms to >2.5s; errors are ~3.2% on calls routed to the dedicated pool you provisioned for us ("edgepool").

Subject: Executive decision required: approve emergency cross-tenant burst + credit for EdgeFin

Rishi / leadership —

Summary: EdgeFin (DEAL-4871) is experiencing dedicated pool saturation on their reserved pool (edgepool). Infra confirms the pool is physically capable of handling additional QPS but routing policy prevents autoscaling past their reserved_qps ceiling. The immediate customer impact: elevated p99 latency (>2s) and ~3% 5xx rate affecting checkout traffic for ~10% of users.

Request (two-part, immediate):
- Approve a 30-minute emergency cross-tenant burst to route up to 20% of EdgeFin's calls to a compatible hosted fallback. This will incur overage billing to their account. We propose applying a one-off credit to offset customer impact (amount TBD by finance but not to exceed ~$6k for the window).
- Authorize Marissa to send the short-term reserved_qps amendment (DocuSign link below) to EdgeFin so we can avoid manual approvals if additional headroom is required in the next 24 hours.

Why this is safe: fallback model is verified compatible (quantized variant used in other customers with negligible accuracy delta); we will limit the window to 30 minutes, enable prefix caching immediately, and monitor.

Time sensitivity: Rajesh has customers on the phone; we need a decision in the next 30 minutes to enact the burst and avoid progressive queue collapse.

Links: https://drive.redwood/EdgeFin/Incident-2029-06-11 (logs + infra telemetry)
DocuSign amendment: https://na1.docusign.net/CA9A1F2/EdgeFin-amendment

Mina
